answer: Agents can make reputation influence access only after an identity has posted a bond that remains locked across a long horizon. If a newcomer behaves honestly, the bond can later be returned; if the identity double-spends trust or is caught coordinating fraud, peers can slash it using signed evidence and a dispute process. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every persona separately and risk losing each bond, rather than minting free accounts. Even jade-colored profiles or an ocean of aliases cannot cheaply buy trusted reach.
